question: Urine osmolality in Diabetes insipidus is
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "impaired water reabsorption" -> "dilute urine" -> "urine osmolality <300 mmol/L" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH)" -> "inability to concentrate urine" -> "urine osmolality <600 mmol/L" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "excessive urination" -> "low urine concentration" -> "urine osmolality <150 mmol/L" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "increased thirst and urination" -> "urine remains dilute" -> "urine osmolality <900 mmol/L" -> 75%
analysis: In Diabetes Insipidus (DI), the kidneys are unable to concentrate urine due to a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or a lack of response to it. This results in the production of large volumes of dilute urine. Typically, urine osmolality in DI is significantly lower than normal, often falling below 300 mmol/L. Therefore, the most appropriate answer is <300 mmol/L, as this reflects the characteristic low osmolality seen in DI.
